path; and an existing sample destination. Check input byte identity after
successful and failed reads. Never demonstrate these cases by overwriting a
source log with a sample.

The contracts cover 256 independent record patterns, 2,048 single-byte
corruptions, exact lengths/null outputs and previous output preservation.
They also demonstrate an undetectable balanced XOR change so the stated
checksum limit is testable. Native CLI checks exercise real files and failures.

predictions, unchanged input files, rejected corruption/truncation, explicit
sample creation and an explanation of EOF versus read failure. An instructor
can walk through the same eight-byte record and FILE loop.

accidental-error check. Define migration and compatibility rules rather than
silently changing the existing eight-byte format.

# CSE9 Capstone Telemetry Transform CLI

This required capstone validates supplied telemetry, performs fixed-point
transforms and emits a normalized CSV. It combines earlier representation,
whole-input parsing, range checks, numerical reasoning and FILE-based work.
Existing input is opened for reading; samples are created only on explicit
request, and normal output requires a new path.

Use the C17 build and translation-unit workflow from the opening units.
These labs target Clang or GCC on macOS, Linux or WSL2 with 8-bit bytes,
and require CMake 3.20 or newer. No additional libraries are needed.

Edit and save the selected role in the site editor when its confirmed import
is available. Download and extract that role's ZIP before native compilation.
Keep the learner attempt before opening the separate reference.

## Project CSV grammar

The first line is exactly:

~~~text
sample_id,temp_milli_c,voltage_mv,flags
~~~

Each data line contains exactly four whole ASCII decimal fields separated by
commas. There are no quotes, spaces, comments, fractions, exponents, hexadecimal
fields or additional columns in this project format. This is a defined CSV
subset, not a general CSV parser. Decimal leading zeroes are allowed.
Only temperature can have a leading minus; plus signs are rejected.

| Field | Inclusive range |
| --- | --- |
| sample_id | 0..255 |
| temp_milli_c | -40000..125000 |
| voltage_mv | 0..5000 |
| flags | 0..255 |

The supplied line reader accepts LF or CRLF and a final line without a
newline. It removes a terminal CR, rejects embedded null bytes and consumes
an entire overlong line before reporting failure. A logical line can contain
at most 127 bytes after removing its line ending. Empty data lines are invalid.
A header-only input is valid and has zero records.

## Fixed-point transform and status

A value of 21500 means 21.500 degrees Celsius. Compute Fahrenheit milli-units
without converting the source to floating point:

~~~text
temp_milli_f = truncate_toward_zero(temp_milli_c * 9 / 5) + 32000
~~~

Validate the Celsius range before arithmetic and use a wide intermediate.
The output range is -40000..257000. Division discards a fractional milli-unit
rather than rounding to nearest; for -1 milli-Celsius the result is 31999
milli-Fahrenheit. Explain this small rounding effect explicitly.

Status is cold below 0 milli-Celsius, hot above 60000 and normal otherwise.
Exactly 0 and 60000 are normal. Flags remain one byte and print as two
hexadecimal digits; this utility preserves their value rather than claiming
to implement an encryption or other flag-controlled behavior.

## Files and two tasks

Each role contains main.c (supplied complete file workflow), telemetry.h,
telemetry.c, tests.c and CMakeLists.txt, plus this complete README.

1. Implement parse_telemetry_row. Use the supplied decimal_field helper to
   consume all four fields and enforce their ranges. Reject null arguments,
   empty/overlong spans, malformed or extra fields and any trailing text.
   Construct a temporary TelemetryRow, then commit output only on success.
2. Implement transform_telemetry_row. Reject null arguments and invalid
   temperature/voltage ranges before arithmetic. Preserve previous output
   on rejection. Copy the validated input fields, calculate Fahrenheit with
   a wide intermediate and classify status, then commit the complete result.

Return TELEMETRY_OK, TELEMETRY_INVALID or the learner's
TELEMETRY_UNFINISHED marker. Keep the interface, supplied bounded field reader,
file driver and contracts unchanged while completing these two functions.

## Build, run and expected unfinished behavior

~~~sh

cmake --build build-starter
ctest --test-dir build-starter --output-on-failure
./build-starter/cse9_capstone_transform_starter
~~~

The untouched learner compiles, but its contract test fails and the normal
program invocation exits 78 with an unfinished diagnostic and no report.
Complete the named tasks, rebuild, then rerun the tests and program.
Save that attempt before opening the separate reference:

~~~sh

cmake --build build-solution
ctest --test-dir build-solution --output-on-failure
./build-solution/cse9_capstone_transform_solution
~~~

Replace clang with gcc for GCC. On Windows use the corresponding .exe.
A sanitizer configuration adds -DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON. Also configure a separate
build with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release; contract checks stay active there.
Both role folders build independently. Invalid command syntax exits 2.

## Demo and existing files

Zero arguments read the supplied fixture through temporary streams and print
normalized CSV directly. This demo creates no persistent input/output files.
Two positional arguments read an existing input and create a new output.
--sample plus a new path explicitly creates the supplied input fixture.

~~~sh

./build-solution/cse9_capstone_transform_solution --sample lesson-input.csv
./build-solution/cse9_capstone_transform_solution lesson-input.csv lesson-output.csv
~~~

The --sample helper is supplied and can work before learner tasks are complete.
Normal demo/transform invocations exit 78 until both tasks work. Malformed CLI
syntax exits 2; input, validation, path and I/O failures exit 1.

The driver validates every input row into temporary output before creating a
named destination. Bad input leaves the source unchanged and creates no output.
An existing destination, the input path itself or an existing sample path is
refused. Failed writes remove only the newly created incomplete destination.
This prevents using sample generation as a hidden replacement for validation.

The normalized schema and default rows are:

~~~text
sample_id,temp_milli_c,temp_milli_f,voltage_mv,flags_hex,status
7,21500,70700,3300,0x05,normal
8,19875,67775,3250,0x01,normal
9,25000,77000,3400,0x81,normal
~~~

Named transforms report the row count after the output is closed successfully.
Line diagnostics count the header as line 1 and the first data row as line 2.

Test both range endpoints, -1/0/1, 60000/60001, flags 0/255, invalid 256,
voltage 5000/5001, a missing header, extra/trailing columns, signed unsigned
fields, very long numbers, embedded null bytes and an overlong line. Try a
bad second row after one good row and confirm that no partial output appears.
Check source bytes after every real-file case. Test an existing output and
input/output equality without changing the original files.

Contracts cover every valid integer Celsius milli-value from -40000 through
125000: 165,001 independently checked transforms, status boundaries,
complete-field grammar, invalid arguments and output preservation. Native
checks additionally verify real file handling, LF/CRLF, final lines, failures,
explicit sample creation and named output preservation in Debug and Release.

predictions, all three default normalized rows, rejected bad input with line
numbers, byte-identical source files and no output created on invalid input.
The same steps form an instructor walkthrough: predict, parse, validate,
transform, check the file and explain the failure boundary.

separate copy. Document its units, range and compatibility; keep the original
schema and tests working while demonstrating the extension.

# Sensor Frame Analyzer Studio

This optional integrative project combines the number-representation, bitwise
and fixed-point units. A sixteen-bit sensor word contains two fields rather
than one signed measurement. Decode the fields, scale the twelve-bit ADC count
and print the original representation alongside its interpretation.

Prerequisites: unsigned shifts and masks, fixed-width integer types, array
capacity, output parameters and integer division. Use Clang or GCC with C17,
8-bit bytes and CMake 3.20+. No extra library is needed. Save the learner
attempt before opening the separate reference. The site editor saves source;
download and extract the selected role before native compilation.

## Word format and calibration

Bits 15..12 encode channel 0..15. Bits 11..0 encode ADC count 0..4095. All
sixteen-bit words are valid. The channel is `raw / 4096`, equivalently an
unsigned shift by twelve. The count is `raw % 4096`, equivalently a mask with
`0x0FFF`. Keep the original word so its bits can be reconstructed from both
fields: `channel * 4096 + count`.

The reference voltage is a whole value in 1..5000 millivolts. Count zero maps
to zero and count 4095 maps to that reference. For other counts:

```text
product = count * reference_mv
millivolts = (product + 2047) / 4095
```

This rounds to the nearest integer. The odd denominator means an exact
half-millivolt tie cannot occur. Widen an operand before multiplication: the
largest product is 20,475,000, which fits `uint32_t` but exceeds `uint16_t`.
A cast after an overflowing narrow product cannot recover the lost bits.

The displayed little-endian bytes are constructed from the integer's low and
high eight bits. They are an explicit byte format, independent of the machine's
in-memory byte order. The bit string contains exactly sixteen high-to-low bits
plus a zero terminator, so its destination needs at least seventeen bytes.

## Files and three tasks

Each selected role contains five files plus this unchanged guide:

- `sensor.h` defines `SensorFrame`, the result enum and complete public contracts.
- `sensor.c` contains the three marked functions to complete.
- `main.c` supplies argument parsing and the formatted report.
- `tests.c` supplies always-active checks, including Release builds.
- `CMakeLists.txt` builds the program and its separate contract executable.

1. Complete `decode_sensor_frame`. Reject a null output. Separate the channel
   and count, then commit a temporary `SensorFrame` containing all three fields.
2. Complete `adc_count_to_mv`. The supplied guard rejects count above 4095,
   reference zero or above 5000, and null output. Apply widened arithmetic and
   the rounding rule. Rejected calls preserve a non-null output value.
3. Complete `format_bits16`. The supplied guard rejects null storage or capacity
   below seventeen without writing. Construct the full string, including its
   terminator, then copy only those seventeen bytes. Leave additional capacity
   untouched. Do not treat a partially written string as a successful result.

## Build, run and the initial failure

From the extracted project folder:

```sh
cmake -S starter -B build-starter -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build-starter
ctest --test-dir build-starter --output-on-failure
./build-starter/cse14_sensor_frame_starter
```

The untouched starter compiles. Its contract test fails and valid normal
execution exits 78 without a report until all three tasks work. Malformed
arguments exit 2 before those tasks. Reference commands use `solution`,
`build-solution` and executable `cse14_sensor_frame_solution`.

Zero arguments select word `0xAABC` and reference 3300 mV. One argument changes
the word; a second changes the reference. Both arguments are complete decimal
or `0x`/`0X` hexadecimal tokens. Leading decimal zeros remain decimal. Empty,
signed, whitespace-containing, fractional, trailing-junk and out-of-range
tokens are rejected. The supplied driver checks printing and final flushing.

The completed default report is:

```text
frame: 0xAABC
bytes (little endian): BC AA
bits: 1010101010111100
channel: 10
ADC count: 2748
voltage: 2215 mV
```

Compare zero, `0x0FFF`, `0xF000` and `0xFFFF`. Predict which field changes
before running each case. At reference 5000, `0xFFFF` reports channel 15,
count 4095 and voltage 5000 mV. A word of 65536 or reference zero is invalid.

## Checks and completion evidence

The contracts inspect all 65,536 words, reconstruct the number from each bit
string, check twelve-bit calibration across three references and verify guard
bytes and rejected-output preservation. Keep the checks enabled. Use:

```sh
cmake -S starter -B build-sanitized -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON
cmake --build build-sanitized
ctest --test-dir build-sanitized --output-on-failure
```

Completion evidence: named function implementations, normal/sanitized test
results, the default report, four boundary predictions, and an explanation of
the representation versus field interpretation. A course facilitator can walk
through one word, one rounded quotient and one rejected call using the same
sequence. Transfer practice changes the frame data; extension practice changes
the analysis or integrity requirement while keeping this documented format.

# Aligned Byte-Region Planner Studio

This optional integrative project turns alignment, capacity and overflow
reasoning into a checked layout plan. It places several requested byte regions
in one logical span, then distinguishes region bytes from alignment gaps.
The program computes offsets; allocation and construction of typed objects
are separate responsibilities. A future allocation needs a base address that
meets the requested alignments as well as sufficient storage.

Prerequisites: `size_t`, array bounds, remainders, output parameters, member
layout observations and failure preservation. Use C17, Clang or GCC and CMake
3.20+. The site editor saves source; extract the selected role's ZIP for native
compilation. Keep the attempt before opening the separate reference.

## Placement contract

A request contains one to eight regions. Every length is positive. Alignment
is a power of two in 1..64: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64. These are explicit
planning requirements, not measured `sizeof` or `_Alignof` values for a type.

Begin at cursor zero. For a region with alignment `a`, calculate `cursor % a`.
If the remainder is zero, add no padding; otherwise add `a - remainder`.
The aligned cursor is the region offset. Add the requested length to obtain
the next cursor. This plan has no trailing alignment padding after its final
region. `total` is the final cursor; `padding` is the sum of intervening gaps.

Check each addition before performing it. Adding `amount` is representable
only when `amount <= SIZE_MAX - cursor`. Do not use `(cursor + a - 1)` first
and check its already-wrapped result afterward. Invalid requests return
`REGION_INVALID`, representational overflow returns `REGION_OVERFLOW`, and a
representable plan larger than the supplied limit returns `REGION_NO_SPACE`.
Each failure leaves the entire output plan unchanged.

A byte position has one of three meanings:

- Inside a region: return `REGION_OK` with its index and relative offset.
- Inside the total span but between regions: return `REGION_PADDING`.
- At or beyond `total`: return `REGION_OUTSIDE`.

Padding, outside and invalid results leave the address output unchanged.
`region_plan_valid` is supplied. It checks bounds, alignment, ordering, count,
total and padding consistency before location lookup. It does not dereference
storage at a calculated address.

## Files and two tasks

Each role includes `regions.h`, `regions.c`, `main.c`, `tests.c`,
`CMakeLists.txt` and this guide. The header defines specifications, placements,
the full plan, addresses and result enum. The driver supplies fixed requests
and collects every location result before printing. The contracts remain
active in Debug and Release.

1. Complete `plan_regions` in `regions.c`. The initial guards validate the
   request. Build a local plan, checking padding and length additions before
   changing the cursor. Compare the completed total with the limit, then
   assign the output once. Do not expose a half-constructed plan on failure.
2. Complete `locate_region`. The initial guard rejects invalid plans and null
   output. Check the total boundary and ordered region spans. Commit the index
   and relative byte only for a contained position; distinguish gaps from
   positions beyond the span.

## Build and observe

From the extracted project folder:

```sh
cmake -S starter -B build-starter -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build-starter
ctest --test-dir build-starter --output-on-failure
./build-starter/cse15_region_planner_starter
```

The untouched learner compiles, its contract fails and normal execution exits
78 without a report. The program takes no arguments; extra arguments exit 2.
The reference uses `solution`, `build-solution` and
`cse15_region_planner_solution`. After completion, the default report is:

```text
region 0: offset=0 length=8 alignment=4
region 1: offset=8 length=3 alignment=1
region 2: offset=16 length=8 alignment=8
total=24 padding=5
byte 0: region=0 relative=0
byte 10: region=1 relative=2
byte 11: padding
byte 16: region=2 relative=0
byte 24: outside
```

Draw the intervals before running. Region 1 ends at byte 11 exclusively, and
bytes 11..15 are padding. Total 24 is a length, so byte 24 is outside. A limit
of 23 rejects this otherwise representable plan. A region of length SIZE_MAX
and alignment one can be represented at offset zero when the limit permits
it; a subsequent positive length or required padding overflows.

## Verification and walkthrough

The tests build hundreds of varied layouts using an independent incrementing
alignment model. They check every byte in and just beyond each layout, padding
classification, insufficient limits, malformed requests, overflow and unchanged
failure outputs. They never allocate SIZE_MAX bytes: the extreme cases test
arithmetic plans only. Run a diagnostic build with
`-DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON` and keep the strict warnings and checks enabled.

Completion evidence: the two implementations, passing normal and diagnostic
contracts, the default interval drawing, an overflowing request prediction and
a rejected-output preservation check. A course facilitator can trace cursor,
gap and exclusive end through the same three regions. Transfer practice changes
region order; extension practice evaluates another alignment or capacity policy
with its own declared contract before adding it to the maintained planner.

# Incremental Binary Frame Decoder Studio

This optional integrative project combines explicit formats, bounded buffers,
callbacks and stream-state reasoning. A frame can arrive across several reads;
a read can also contain the end of one frame and the start of another. Preserve
that state instead of assuming one read equals one record.

Prerequisites: fixed packet parsing, `FILE *`, checked I/O, pointer-plus-length
spans and function pointers. Use C17 on an 8-bit-byte Clang/GCC platform with
CMake 3.20+. The browser edits and saves source; download and extract the chosen
role. Save the attempt before comparing the separate reference.

## Byte format and checksum

Each frame contains `A5`, version `01`, payload length 0..32, that many payload
bytes, then one CRC byte. Total frame length is 4..36 bytes. Payload bytes are
arbitrary binary data, including zero. Length zero is a valid frame. No native
struct is written or read as the wire representation.

CRC processing includes magic, version, length and payload, excluding the final
CRC byte. Start at zero. XOR each input byte into the current CRC, then process
eight bits high first: shift left once, XOR polynomial `0x07` when the outgoing
high bit was one, and retain the low eight bits. There is no reflection or final
XOR. `crc8_update` supplies this algorithm. The byte string `123456789` yields
CRC `F4`; the test also compares every previous-CRC/input-byte pair with an
independent polynomial-division model. CRC detects accidental changes and does
not provide authentication.

The temporary demo and explicit sample helper produce eleven bytes:

```text
A5 01 03 10 00 FF 53 A5 01 00 9D
```

The first frame has payload `10 00 FF`, the second has an empty payload.

## Decoder state and callback ownership

`stream_init` supplies a zeroed decoder with a non-null callback and its context.
It owns its 32-byte scratch array and no allocation. Input spans must be valid
and disjoint from the decoder. A callback cannot re-enter or mutate the decoder.
Its payload pointer is borrowed only for that call; copy bytes needed later.

| State | Next byte and action |
| --- | --- |
| Magic | Accept A5 and start the CRC |
| Version | Accept 01 and extend the CRC |
| Length | Accept 0..32; choose payload or checksum |
| Payload | Save one bounded byte and extend the CRC |
| Checksum | Compare CRC, call the callback, count success and reset to magic |
| Failed | Preserve the stored failure result |

Bad magic, unsupported version, length above 32 or wrong checksum fail the
decoder. A false callback result produces `STREAM_CALLBACK_ERROR`. A frame
counter already at SIZE_MAX produces `STREAM_LIMIT` before calling it. Prior
accepted frames stay accepted; an invalid later frame is not delivered. The
library provides frame-level acceptance. The supplied file driver separately
stages the report and prints only after the entire input passes.

`stream_finish` inspects EOF: magic state is a complete boundary; a partial
header, payload or checksum returns `STREAM_TRUNCATED`; a failed state returns
its recorded error. It does not seal or change the decoder. Empty input has
zero valid frames. Invalid pointer/span arguments are rejected without mutation.

## Files and two tasks

Each role includes `stream.h`, `stream.c`, `main.c`, `tests.c`,
`CMakeLists.txt` and this guide. The header defines the public state and callback
signature. `stream.c` supplies initialization, CRC and representation checks.

1. Complete `stream_feed`. Retain partial state between calls, validate each
   byte at its proper stage and invoke the callback only after a full frame's
   checksum succeeds. Reset the next-frame state only after callback success.
2. Complete `stream_finish`. Distinguish a complete boundary, truncation and
   each stored failure. Repeated inspection must not change the decoder.

## Independent build and file workflow

From the extracted project directory:

```sh
cmake -S starter -B build-starter -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build-starter
ctest --test-dir build-starter --output-on-failure
./build-starter/cse16_stream_decoder_starter
```

The untouched learner compiles, fails its contract and exits 78 without a normal
report. Reference commands use `solution`, `build-solution` and
`cse16_stream_decoder_solution`. A diagnostic build adds
`-DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON`; test it separately and keep the bounds checks enabled.

Zero arguments use a temporary demonstration. One argument reads an existing
file in binary read-only mode. `--sample NEWpath` explicitly creates the sample
and refuses an existing path; this supplied helper works even before learner
tasks are completed. CLI-shape errors exit 2; content and I/O errors exit 1.
There is no automatic recreation of input. The completed default output is:

```text
frame 1 (3 bytes): 10 00 FF
frame 2 (0 bytes):
valid frames: 2
```

## Checks and completion evidence

The tests vary every split of a multi-frame stream, retain empty and maximum
payloads, cut every position of a full frame, corrupt every byte and check EOF,
callback rejection, counter limits and argument preservation. Predict what
remains in decoder state after each of the driver's five-byte reads. Then
distinguish accepted prior frames in the library from the file driver's staged
report after a later error. Invalid complete input produces no report; a failing
stdout write can interrupt delivery after validation and is reported as I/O failure.

Completion evidence: both implementations, normal/diagnostic contracts, the
sample report, a chunk-state trace, unchanged input bytes and rejection of one
truncated and one corrupt file. The same state table supports a facilitator
walkthrough. Transfer practice changes chunk boundaries; extension practice
compares a declared framing or checksum policy without silently changing version 1.

# Telemetry Time-Window Aggregator Studio

This optional capstone studio combines strict CSV parsing, bounded storage,
ordering contracts, integer arithmetic and complete-input validation. It groups
timestamped temperature samples into fixed time windows, then reports count,
mean, minimum and maximum. Its purpose is multi-row aggregation rather than
the required utility's independent per-row unit conversion.

Prerequisites: the telemetry utility, array bounds, `uint32_t`, `int32_t`,
`int64_t`, output parameters and checked I/O. Use C17, Clang/GCC and CMake 3.20+.
Edit and save the selected role in the site editor, then extract its ZIP for
native compilation. Keep the attempt before opening the separate reference.

## Input grammar and limits

The first line is exactly `timestamp_ms,temp_milli_c`. Each subsequent line has
two whole ASCII decimal fields, separated by one comma. Timestamp is in
0..4294967295. Temperature is in -40000..125000 milli-degrees Celsius. Leading
zeros are decimal. A minus is accepted only on temperature; plus, spaces,
quotes, hexadecimal, fractions, extra columns and embedded zero bytes are
invalid. There are no blank data rows.

The driver accepts LF, CRLF and a final line without a newline. Each line is at
most 95 bytes after its supported line ending is removed. It reads at most
256 data rows; a further row is rejected. A header-only file is valid and has
zero buckets. An empty file has no required header and is invalid. Existing
input is opened read-only and is never recreated as a sample.

Timestamps must be nondecreasing. Equal timestamps are allowed and contribute
separate samples. Sorting is not performed silently. The aggregation API
rechecks temperature range and ordering even for directly constructed samples.

## Window and mean contracts

Window width is a positive whole number of milliseconds, at most UINT32_MAX.
Default width is 1000. Bucket start is `timestamp - timestamp % width`, or the
mathematically equivalent rounded-down multiple. This calculation avoids a
potentially overflowing 32-bit bucket-end addition near UINT32_MAX.

All rows with that start share a bucket. Sum temperatures in `int64_t`, then
divide by the positive count. C integer division truncates toward zero: the
mean of -1 and 0 milli-degrees is 0, not -1. The limits bound the sum to at most
32,000,000 in magnitude and the mean stays inside the accepted temperature range.
Minimum and maximum retain the observed extrema.

The output buffer has a caller-declared bucket capacity. Invalid arguments,
bad fields, descending time and insufficient capacity preserve both the entire
output buffer and `used`. Stage results until all validation and capacity checks
succeed. Null input/output spans are valid only with zero count/capacity; a
non-null `used` and positive width are always needed. Empty input then succeeds
with `used = 0`.

## Files and two tasks

Each role contains `window.h`, `window.c`, `main.c`, `tests.c`,
`CMakeLists.txt` and this guide. The header defines sample, bucket and result
types. The supplied decimal helper checks range before multiplication.

1. Complete `parse_sample_row`. Split exactly two fields, validate both complete
   tokens and their ranges, then commit a temporary `Sample`. Do not accept a
   numeric prefix followed by junk or overwrite a previous output on failure.
2. Complete `aggregate_samples`. Validate spans, width, count, ranges and order.
   Group contiguous equal bucket starts, calculate statistics with widened
   sums, check capacity and commit only the successful results.

## Build, run and sample handling

From the extracted project folder:

```sh
cmake -S starter -B build-starter -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build-starter
ctest --test-dir build-starter --output-on-failure
./build-starter/cse17_window_aggregator_starter
```

The untouched starter compiles, its contract fails and a normal invocation
exits 78 without a report. Reference commands use `solution`, `build-solution`
and `cse17_window_aggregator_solution`. A diagnostic build adds
`-DCSE_SANITIZERS=ON`; checks remain active in Release as well.

Zero arguments use temporary demo input. One argument reads an existing CSV;
a second sets decimal width. `--sample NEWpath` explicitly creates sample input
and refuses an existing path. The supplied helper already works before the
learner tasks. CLI-shape or width errors exit 2; input, ordering, capacity and
I/O failures exit 1. Printing starts after complete input validation. A write
failure can interrupt the report and is still reported as an I/O failure.

The default input is:

```csv
timestamp_ms,temp_milli_c
999,-1
1000,1000
1500,2000
2001,60001
```

The completed default report is:

```csv
bucket_ms,count,mean_milli_c,min_milli_c,max_milli_c
0,1,-1,-1,-1
1000,2,1500,1000,2000
2000,1,60001,60001,60001
```

## Predictions and completion evidence

The contracts compare varied ordered datasets with an independent segment
model, check decimal grammar and signed rounding, reach UINT32_MAX and preserve
outputs on failure. Predict the effect of width one, width 2000, duplicate time,
one reversed pair and a malformed final row. Check that the final-row failure
starts no report and leaves the input bytes unchanged.

the three default buckets, a changed-width report, negative-mean reasoning,
ordering rejection and an input-preservation check. A course facilitator can
walk through one boundary and one two-row mean before reviewing the full file.
Transfer practice changes time/temperature cases; extension practice proposes
another explicitly documented aggregation policy with its own tests.
